title: Hazel and the Wolf
premise: Marguerite Thornbury, a temple scribe bound by debt to the godless valley of Ashenmere, has spent his life copying wards he cannot use, for magic dies at the valley's edge. When the border wards collapse and the stars go out on the same night, Marguerite is seized by the Wolf — an exiled war-mage wearing the body of a dying soldier — who needs a scribe's true-name craft to rewrite the ancient covenant that once ended the mage wars. As they flee toward the ruined capital through a winter that will not end, Marguerite discovers the Wolf's secret: the covenant can only be renewed with a willing sacrifice, and the Wolf intends it to be himself. In the end, Marguerite chooses love over duty, offering his own name instead; the Wolf refuses, they split the cost between them, and the stars return dimmed but burning — leaving both alive, changed, and no longer what they were.
about_author: W. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction full-time. Hartwell writes fantasy about bargains, bureaucracy, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet him ink-stained and debt-bound in the temple scriptorium of Ashenmere, copying ward-charters he'll never be permitted to cast. A small act of forgery to buy his mother's medicine establishes his desperation and skill. Emotional beat: quiet resentment beneath dutiful calm.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The border wards shatter at dusk; by midnight every star above the valley is dark. Panic spreads as refugees from beyond the mountains arrive speaking of a walking winter. Marguerite is conscripted to copy emergency dispatches. Emotional beat: dread curdling into awe.

chapters.title: What Came Through the Wards
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Among the refugees hides a wounded soldier who collapses at the temple steps — and whose eyes burn silver when no one watches. He whispers one word to Marguerite: 'scribe.' The temple elders order the stranger held. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Door
chapters.summary: The Wolf's POV, first time. We learn the soldier is a shell: the Wolf, exiled war-mage, wears him to survive the wardless valley where his own magic gutters. He needs a name-craftsman to reach the old capital's covenant-stone before midwinter. Emotional beat: cold calculation shadowed by exhaustion.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Ink
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Wolf offers to erase Marguerite's debt-bond in exchange for his services as scribe on the journey. The temple elders refuse to release him; the Wolf takes the choice away, spiriting them both out during the evacuation. Emotional beat: fury and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Ashenmere
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They cross the dead wards into a landscape where magic seeps back like frostbite — Marguerite feels it for the first time and hates how much he wants it. First skirmish with starless wights hunting the darkness. Emotional beat: wonder weaponized into survival.

chapters.title: Lessons in Borrowed Fire
chapters.summary: The Wolf's POV. Traveling by night, the Wolf teaches Marguerite rudimentary ward-script, hiding how fast the borrowed body is failing. Marguerite proves unnervingly gifted. Their banter softens into something neither names. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Village That Prayed Wrong
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A roadside village worships the darkened sky as a god's silence and offers travelers to it. Marguerite talks them down with forged scripture — his forgery skill turned to mercy. The Wolf watches, unsettled by being saved by lies. Emotional beat: power's seduction examined.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Covenant
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The Order of the Unbroken Star — zealots who broke the wards — ambush them, believing the Wolf must die before he reaches the covenant-stone. First revelation: the Wolf helped write the original covenant, and its price was hidden even then. Emotional beat: betrayal of trust in institutions.

chapters.title: Wounds That Remember
chapters.summary: The Wolf's POV. Sheltering in a ruined watchtower, the Wolf's host-body begins dying faster; each healing spell burns years off it. Marguerite finds the Wolf's true name scratched into the tower wall by his own hand, centuries ago. Emotional beat: intimacy through vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Temple enforcers catch up, demanding their property back. To protect the Wolf, Marguerite signs himself deeper into bondage — trading his freedom for their escape. The Wolf is furious; Marguerite realizes he chose this. Emotional beat: duty and love pulling apart.

chapters.title: Midwinter Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They traverse the frozen pass where the first war was fought, littered with petrified soldiers still locked in combat. The Wolf confesses fragments: the covenant didn't end the war, it froze it, and the frozen are waking. Emotional beat: horror as history, not legend.

chapters.title: The City Under Snow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They reach the half-buried capital, where survivors live in candlelit undercrofts ruled by a council of mages gone soft and cruel. The council recognizes the Wolf and offers hospitality with chains attached. Emotional beat: safety revealed as another cage.

chapters.title: Council of Ashes
chapters.summary: The Wolf's POV. Before the council, the Wolf learns the truth he fled from: renewing the covenant requires a willing sacrifice bearing a crafted true-name — which is why he needed a scribe. He had always intended himself. The council wants Marguerite instead. Emotional beat: guilt igniting into resolve.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Read in the Dark
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Left alone with the covenant archives, Marguerite deciphers the original text and finds the Wolf's centuries-old annotation: 'let it be me.' He understands the whole journey was the Wolf's slow walk to his own execution. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The starless dark breaches the city walls; the frozen army wakes in the streets. The council flees or falls. Marguerite and the Wolf fight side by side through burning snow to reach the covenant-stone beneath the citadel. Emotional beat: chaos forging certainty.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Stone
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the stone, the Wolf begins the rite with his own name — and Marguerite overwrites it with his own, having spent chapters secretly crafting himself as the sacrifice. The magic accepts the substitution. The Wolf screams no. Emotional beat: love as the ultimate transgression.

chapters.title: The Price Split in Two
chapters.summary: The Wolf's POV. Rather than let Marguerite die alone, the Wolf tears the covenant open and forces the cost to divide — half a name, half a life, each. The ritual completes imperfectly: the stars return, dimmed, and the waking dead lie down again. Both survive, diminished. Emotional beat: devastation transformed into shared survival.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The valley's wards reknit; Ashenmere sends envoys to a world that has changed. Marguerite's debt-bond burned with the old covenant — he is free and doesn't know what freedom is for. The Wolf, mortal now and aging, convalesces. Emotional beat: disorientation of peace.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Winter turns. Marguerite returns to the scriptorium but cannot resume the old life; the Wolf cannot leave without him. Neither will say it aloud, so they write letters neither delivers — until Marguerite burns them all and packs a bag. Emotional beat: longing outrunning pride.

chapters.title: The Choice Beyond the Wards
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite walks out of the valley willingly — the first person ever to choose the magical world over the safe one — and finds the Wolf waiting at the border stones, having made the mirror choice to stay near. No bargain this time. Emotional beat: love chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, closing frame. Spring comes wrong but it comes. Together they take work rewriting the broken covenants of the world — two flawed scribes of a new accord, half-named, wholly bound by choice rather than debt. Final image: the first true starrise over the pass. Emotional beat: hard-won, unglamorous hope.
